keyRecoveries.BridgeActivitySnapshot: Generic in the presentation payload. Only discoverable from the author's use site (bridge-tool-dispatcher.ts:126); nothing in the JavaScript reveals the generic arity.
keyRecoveries.FileToolContext.workspaceRoots: Allowed to be a thunk, because invokeFileTool resolves it lazily so root-resolution failures are enveloped as tool errors rather than thrown. The author relies on this ('Lazy on purpose').
keyRecoveries.FileToolResult.content: Optional, evidenced by the author's `result.content ?? [...]` fallback; a mandatory field would make that dead code.
keyRecoveries.SkillLoadDiagnosis: Modelled as a discriminated union on `loaded`. The author's own code (bridge-server.ts:308-318) both maps over it and hand-builds a failing entry that still carries `name`, which is why the failure branch keeps name optional rather than omitting it.
keyRecoveries.findCustomTool: Returns CustomToolManifest | undefined - not a guess: the author's wrapper at bridge-tool-dispatcher.ts:219 declares exactly that return type. Disabled tools are invisible to it, so a caller cannot accidentally execute one.
keyRecoveries.BridgeSessionRegistry: Generic in the session type: the author writes BridgeSessionRegistry<McpSession> (bridge-mcp-transport.ts:183,202). The destroy reason is deliberately a widened string, not a closed union - the module emits four values but the author passes 'bridge-shutdown' and 'initialize-error' from the extension, so a closed union would reject their own code.
keyRecoveries.Semaphore.setLimit: Lowering the ceiling never revokes a held permit, so `active` can legitimately exceed `limit` until in-flight work drains. Documented on the type because callers must not assume active <= limit.
keyRecoveries.SkillRunnerResult: Discriminated union on `generated`: runnerRel exists only on the generated branch, so reading it forces a check first. The JS returns two differently-shaped literals (lines 157 and 160), which a single optional-field interface would have flattened and lost.
keyRecoveries.parseBridgePlan: Assigns positional ids plan-1, plan-2 on every call. A plan is replaced wholesale rather than patched, so the ids are deliberately not stable across calls.
keyRecoveries.normalizeFileToolInput: Returns unknown, not a record. The author's own cast at bridge-tool-dispatcher.ts:301 ('as Record<string, unknown>') is the evidence: the function passes non-objects straight through, so typing the return as a record would contradict their code.
keyRecoveries.validateToolInput: Validates by throwing; it returns void, not a verdict. Also worth stating on the type: it enforces only a subset of JSON Schema (type/enum/length/range/required/properties/items/additionalProperties). $ref, oneOf, allOf, anyOf, pattern and format are silently accepted, so callers must not assume full coverage.

q3_monetisation.architectureFound: The client never touches payment. bridge-license-service.ts:396 POSTs {planId, paymentType} to a Cloudflare Worker (shuncode-bridge-license.2357872806.workers.dev), receives a checkoutUrl, validates it, opens it with openExternal(), and polls the order. Sign-in is Gitee OAuth with a 127.0.0.1 loopback callback.
q3_monetisation.answerToPortingQuestion: The assistant on the other project is right that WeChat Pay needs a merchant ID. ShunCode does not avoid that requirement - it relocates it to the server. The merchant account still has to exist behind the Worker; only the client is freed from handling credentials. What is portable is the pattern: client receives a checkoutUrl and nothing else, payment channel is a parameter, OAuth replaces a bespoke account system.
q3_monetisation.caveat: The Worker's own source is NOT in this repository. Server-side Alipay integration lives in the author's Cloudflare account.

q4_chat_fields_impact.proof: Two greps came back empty: no file outside tool-presentation.ts reads .items/.metrics/.diffPreview/.presentationKind/.presentationStyle, and no B-layer module references them. They are constructed in one function and handed to vscode.ChatToolInvocationPart.toolSpecificData (native-chat.ts:559,582). No logic branches on them.
